paragraphs: Language models can improve because researchers spend more computation or because training methods make better use of that computation. This paper estimates these contributions separately. It studies more than 200 evaluations on Wikitext and Penn Treebank, covering 2012–2023, to ask how quickly algorithms reduced the computation needed for a fixed level of performance.

The authors fit augmented scaling laws that account for both computational scale and algorithmic improvements. They estimate that the computation required to reach a given performance threshold halved roughly every eight months. The uncertainty is substantial: their 90% confidence interval ranges from about two to 22 months. The estimated pace nevertheless exceeds hardware improvement associated with Moore's Law.

Fast algorithmic progress does not mean algorithms explain most of the observed gains. The analysis attributes an even larger contribution to increased computation, despite innovations such as transformers. Because the benchmark observations are noisy, these results are estimates of historical contributions, with uncertainty, rather than a precise timetable for future progress.
neurips-2024-algorithmic-progress-in-lan.tldr: Historical benchmark analysis estimates rapid algorithmic efficiency gains, while finding that increased computation contributed even more to language-model performance improvements.

paragraphs: Learning from video and accompanying audio depends on how well the two sources match. Background sounds and timing mismatches can weaken the relationship that a model is supposed to learn. This paper addresses that problem through data preparation, using an automated assistant called AVAgent to adjust audio so that it better corresponds to visual content.

AVAgent first uses a multimodal language model to describe the audio and video separately in language. It reasons about whether those descriptions indicate a good match and plans audio changes when needed. Predefined editing actions perform operations such as noise filtering or augmentation. A vision-language model then evaluates the modified pairing and supplies feedback for another round.

This repeated sequence of description, planning, editing, and feedback gradually aligns the paired data. Existing representation-learning methods can use the resulting examples directly. The authors report state-of-the-art results against previous baselines across diverse downstream tasks, supporting the value of improving the correspondence within training examples as part of learning stronger joint representations.
neurips-2024-aligning-audio-visual-joint.tldr: AVAgent repeatedly evaluates and edits audio to better match video, improving joint representations and downstream task performance.

paragraphs: Machine-learning systems that analyze compiled programs need suitable collections of binary files. Although malicious binaries are widely collected, high-quality benign binaries for modern systems are harder to obtain, partly because of licensing constraints. Assemblage addresses this data problem with infrastructure that automatically discovers software, configures builds, and produces binary datasets.

The system distributes this work through cloud resources and is designed to support reproducible, extensible dataset construction. Users can publish recipes describing how their datasets were produced and extract different kinds of features. The authors report an AWS deployment that generated 890,000 Windows PE binaries and 428,000 Linux ELF binaries across 29 configurations.

To evaluate the resulting data, the researchers trained learning-based systems for identifying compiler provenance and comparing binary functions. These applications test whether the generated collections support practical analysis tasks. The reported findings emphasize the need for robust Windows PE corpora in modern binary-analysis pipelines. The contribution combines a substantial generated resource with a way to construct and describe further datasets reproducibly.
neurips-2024-assemblage-automatic-binary.tldr: Assemblage automates reproducible binary-dataset construction and demonstrates its usefulness for training practical binary-analysis systems.

paragraphs: A pretrained classifier may recognize many categories that an application does not need. This paper studies selective forgetting: reducing recognition of designated categories while preserving accuracy on the others. Its particular challenge is a black-box setting, where the model's architecture, parameters, and gradients are unavailable, preventing the kinds of internal modifications assumed by previous approaches.

The proposed method works through the input prompt. It uses derivative-free optimization to search for prompts that lower accuracy on the classes selected for forgetting. Searching over many prompt tokens would create a difficult high-dimensional optimization problem. Latent Context Sharing reduces that burden by giving multiple tokens common components in a lower-dimensional latent representation.

Experiments on four standard datasets show better performance than the baselines considered by the authors. The contribution is a method for changing selective recognition behavior through prompts under restricted model access. The stated objective concerns classification accuracy on selected and retained categories; the mechanism described in the abstract operates at the input interface rather than modifying the pretrained model's parameters.
neurips-2024-black-box-forgetting-96458a.tldr: Shared low-dimensional prompt components enable selective forgetting in classifiers whose internal parameters and gradients are inaccessible.

paragraphs: Evaluating the values expressed in a language-model response requires judgments that can adapt to human definitions and remain consistent across different wording and situations. An evaluator's own biases can complicate this task. CLAVE addresses these demands by dividing the work between a large language model and a smaller model trained to follow human annotations.

The large model extracts high-level value concepts from responses, using its broader knowledge to handle varied expressions. The smaller model learns how those concepts relate to the human-provided labels. This separates concept extraction from adaptation to a particular value system. The authors describe adaptation using fewer than 100 human-labeled examples for each value type.

The paper also introduces ValEval, containing more than 13,000 text, value, and label combinations across diverse domains and three major value systems. It benchmarks more than 15 language-model evaluators and analyzes their strengths and weaknesses. The findings favor CLAVE's combination of prompted large-model interpretation and smaller-model fine-tuning as a balance between generalization and adaptation in value evaluation.
neurips-2024-clave-an-adaptive-framework.tldr: CLAVE combines large-model concept extraction with a smaller trained evaluator to adapt value judgments using limited human annotation.

paragraphs: Predictive models can help identify individuals of interest within a large candidate pool, but selecting candidates using the data changes the distribution being evaluated. This paper studies how to control the false discovery rate after that selection. The challenge is to construct uncertainty measures that reflect the selected population rather than treating selection as irrelevant.

The method uses a held-out labeled dataset to reproduce the effects of the selection process. It adaptively chooses calibration examples according to the stability of the selection rule. This construction makes the calibration data exchangeable with the selected test unit, providing the symmetry needed to obtain valid conformal p-values.

The resulting p-values are used with the Benjamini-Hochberg procedure to control false discoveries within the selected subset. The theoretical framework accounts for both the randomness of that subset and dependence among the p-values. Numerical studies support the procedures' validity and effectiveness across several scenarios. The central contribution is a way to incorporate selection into calibration so that statistical guarantees remain meaningful for the candidates actually examined.
neurips-2024-conformalized-multiple-test.tldr: Selection-aware calibration enables valid conformal testing and false-discovery control within data-selected candidate subsets.

paragraphs: Continual learning requires incorporating new observations while retaining useful information from earlier ones. This paper approaches that problem by interpreting a single neural-network classifier as a Bayesian ensemble. The motivating idea is that updating weights over fixed predictors offers a principled way to accumulate evidence from successive data without changing the predictors themselves.

The authors show that a network with N parameters can be represented as a weighted collection of N neural tangent experts. Each expert produces a valid probability distribution over labels. In the lazy-regime limit, these experts remain fixed during learning. The paper derives their likelihoods and posterior probabilities given previously observed data.

The resulting Bayesian posterior updates correspond to a scaled and projected version of stochastic gradient descent on the network weights. Outside the lazy regime, the interpretation changes to an ensemble of adaptive experts that improve over time. This connection provides a framework for understanding and mitigating forgetting, while making clear that the fixed-expert interpretation depends on the lazy-regime limit.
neurips-2024-continual-learning-with-the.tldr: A neural network can be interpreted as a Bayesian ensemble whose expert updates connect to modified stochastic gradient descent.

paragraphs: A world model represents an environment so that a reinforcement-learning agent can train within its predictions. Many recent approaches compress observations into discrete latent variables, which may discard visual details relevant to decisions. DIAMOND explores diffusion-based world modeling as a way to preserve useful detail when generating the environments an agent learns from.

The paper examines design choices needed to adapt diffusion generation to this role and demonstrates that better visual detail can improve agent performance. On Atari 100k, DIAMOND achieves a mean human-normalized score of 1.46. The authors report this as a new best result specifically among agents trained entirely inside a world model.

The researchers also train a diffusion world model on recorded Counter-Strike: Global Offensive gameplay and demonstrate it as an interactive neural game engine. Together, the results show two uses of the learned dynamics: supporting agent training and generating an interactive environment. The findings connect the quality of visual modeling to decision-making performance without claiming that every improvement in image detail necessarily improves control.
neurips-2024-diffusion-for-world-modelin.tldr: DIAMOND uses a diffusion world model to preserve useful visual detail and achieves strong Atari performance with agents trained entirely inside that model.

paragraphs: Online continual learning must keep up with a stream that does not stop while a model trains. This paper argues that preventing forgetting is only part of the problem: training throughput determines how many arriving examples the model can actually use. More expensive learning procedures can therefore sacrifice access to data even when they improve retention.

The authors identify two further challenges. Ignorance describes difficulty learning effective features from a single pass under limited time and storage. Myopia describes learning features and an excessively sparse classifier suited to the current task but poorly aligned with the overall objective. Their empirical and theoretical analysis examines these issues alongside forgetting.

The proposed Non-sparse Classifier Evolution framework combines non-sparse maximum-separation regularization with targeted experience replay and pretrained models. It aims to acquire features that distinguish classes across tasks while adding little training time. Experiments report substantial improvements in performance, throughput, and practical applicability. These findings support evaluating continual learners by both the quality of what they learn and their ability to process the available stream.
neurips-2024-forgetting-ignorance-or-myo.tldr: NsCE addresses limited feature learning and task-local myopia alongside forgetting, improving reported accuracy and throughput in online continual learning.

paragraphs: Bounding boxes let users specify where objects should appear in a generated image. GrounDiT provides this spatial control for diffusion transformers without additional training. The paper targets a weakness of earlier training-free techniques: updating a noisy image through custom-loss gradients can struggle to control the contents of individual boxes precisely.

The approach uses a property the authors call semantic sharing. When a small patch is jointly denoised with an image of a size the model can generate, the two acquire matching semantic content. GrounDiT uses this behavior to generate patches that encode the intended objects for particular bounding boxes.

Each patch is denoised in its own generation branch, then inserted into the matching region of the main noisy image at every timestep. Repeated transplantation supplies local object information throughout generation. On HRS and DrawBench, the authors report state-of-the-art performance relative to previous training-free approaches. The contribution is a generation-time mechanism that turns the transformer's patch flexibility into more precise control over individual image regions.
neurips-2024-groundit-grounding-diffusio.tldr: GrounDiT improves training-free object placement by repeatedly transplanting separately denoised object patches into specified image regions.

paragraphs: Predicting future observations or explaining how a system reached its current state can be difficult when each observation has many dimensions. This paper shows how a variant of temporal contrastive learning can produce representations in which such probabilistic questions admit compact, closed-form answers. The focus is on the structure of the learned representation space.

The analysis builds on the result that contrastive representations encode a probability ratio. The authors extend this reasoning by establishing Gaussian marginal distributions over representations and then a Gaussian joint distribution. Together, these results give the representations a Gauss-Markov-chain structure, connecting the learning procedure to a tractable model of temporal dependence.

Within this structure, prediction and planning reduce to inverting a low-dimensional matrix. In one special case, estimating intermediate representations becomes interpolation between learned representations. The authors validate their theory with numerical simulations on tasks with up to 46 dimensions. The interpolation result is explicitly a special case; the broader contribution is a theoretical route from temporal representation learning to efficient probabilistic inference.
neurips-2024-inference-via-interpolation.tldr: A temporal contrastive-learning analysis yields Gaussian representations that support compact inference, with interpolation solving one special case.

paragraphs: Images and videos contain substantial redundancy, so spending the same amount of processing on every visual token can waste computation. Mixture of Nested Experts addresses this by assigning tokens to experts with different computational costs. Its nested experts occupy an increasing compute-accuracy curve, providing multiple levels of processing within the proposed architecture.

Given a computation budget, the model learns a priority order for tokens and routes redundant ones through cheaper experts. This makes the allocation of computation depend on the visual input. The approach targets a gap between standard vision transformers, which do not capitalize on this redundancy, and mixture-of-experts models that carry a larger parameter footprint.

The authors evaluate MoNE on ImageNet-21K, Kinetics400, and Something-Something-v2. They report performance equivalent to baseline models while using less than half the inference computation. A single trained video model also maintains strong performance across different inference budgets. This suggests that adaptive token processing can support both efficiency at a chosen budget and flexibility when the available computation changes.
neurips-2024-mixture-of-nested-experts-a.tldr: MoNE routes visual tokens through nested experts of different costs, matching baseline performance with more than a twofold reduction in inference computation.

paragraphs: Muharaf is a dataset intended to advance recognition of handwritten Arabic and cursive writing more broadly. It contains more than 1,600 images of historical handwritten pages, with transcriptions produced by experts in archival Arabic. The resource pairs visual examples of writing with expert readings, supplying the supervision needed to study recognition on these documents.

The annotations also describe where text appears. Each page includes polygon coordinates for text lines and basic page elements, connecting the transcribed material to its spatial layout. The collection covers varied handwriting styles and document types, including letters, diaries, notes, poems, church records, and legal correspondence. This variety is a central feature of the dataset.

The paper documents how the material was acquired, describes notable properties, and reports dataset statistics. It also provides a preliminary recognition baseline obtained by training convolutional neural networks on the data. That baseline offers an initial reference for subsequent work, while the main contribution is the expert-transcribed, spatially annotated collection itself.
neurips-2024-muharaf-manuscripts-of-hand.tldr: Muharaf provides over 1,600 historical Arabic manuscript pages with expert transcriptions, spatial annotations, and a preliminary recognition baseline.

paragraphs: Generating random molecules is only one part of using generative models for molecular discovery. Researchers also need ways to explore possible structures and move toward desired properties. ChemFlow addresses this by navigating the latent space learned by a molecular generative model, treating exploration as a directed process through that representation.

The framework takes a dynamical-systems perspective. It learns a vector field that moves the molecular distribution toward regions associated with desired properties or structural diversity. This gives a common formulation for earlier approaches to latent-space traversal and optimization. The authors also introduce alternative methods within that framework that incorporate different physical priors.

ChemFlow is evaluated on molecular manipulation and optimization involving either a single objective or multiple objectives. The experiments cover supervised and unsupervised discovery settings and support the framework's effectiveness on those tasks. Its contribution is both a unifying account of how molecular latent spaces can be traversed and a set of competing flow-based methods for directing that traversal toward discovery goals.
neurips-2024-navigating-chemical-space-w.tldr: ChemFlow learns flows through molecular latent spaces to guide exploration toward desired properties or structural diversity.

paragraphs: The paper studies targets that depend on a high-dimensional input only through its projection onto one hidden direction, followed by an unknown function. Under isotropic Gaussian inputs, earlier gradient-based results required sample counts whose dimensional dependence grew with the function's information exponent. That exponent measures the lowest nonzero degree in its Hermite expansion.

The authors prove that a two-layer network trained with an SGD-based squared-loss algorithm can avoid this dependence for polynomial targets. Both sample count and runtime scale as the input dimension times polylogarithmic factors, with constants depending on polynomial degree. This matches the information-theoretic dimension dependence up to those polylogarithmic factors.

The mechanism is reuse of minibatches when computing gradients, which accesses higher-order information beyond correlational queries. More generally, the paper gives a sufficient sample bound governed by a generative exponent no larger than the information exponent. The results explain how the specified training procedure can exceed expectations based on correlational-query lower bounds, within the Gaussian single-index setting analyzed.
neurips-2024-neural-network-learns-low-d.tldr: An SGD-based method using minibatch reuse learns polynomial single-index targets under Gaussian inputs with nearly dimension-linear sample and runtime complexity.

paragraphs: Probabilistic values assign credit to features or data points, but different choices can work better for different downstream tasks. Exact computation is often exponentially expensive, so comparing several choices requires approximation. This paper develops a shared estimation framework intended to make that comparison efficient by reusing samples across different probabilistic values.

Instead of estimating each value separately, the method estimates intermediate quantities that can be converted into any probabilistic value. A sampling vector controls how the shared information is collected. The authors derive a formula governing convergence under a specified accuracy-and-confidence criterion, then optimize that vector to obtain both a general one-for-all estimator and estimators tuned to individual values.

The one-for-all estimator attains the best currently known time complexity averaged across probabilistic values, according to the paper. For Beta Shapley values, including Shapley itself, the authors establish the fastest convergence rate theoretically and empirically. They also connect these values to least-squares datamodels, showing that the shared estimator can solve a family of such models simultaneously.
neurips-2024-one-sample-fits-all-approxi.tldr: A shared sampling framework efficiently approximates multiple probabilistic attribution values and also solves a related family of datamodels.

paragraphs: This paper studies reinforcement learning in Markov decision processes whose transitions use multinomial-logit function approximation. The nonlinear formulation ensures valid probability distributions over states, but creates statistical and computational challenges. An earlier regret bound contained an inverse problem-dependent factor that can grow polynomially with the number of reachable states, weakening the benefit of function approximation.

The proposed algorithm moves that inverse factor out of the leading regret term. Ignoring logarithmic factors, its bound is d H² √K plus κ⁻¹ d² H², where d is feature dimension, H is episode length, and K is episode count. Thus, the term that grows with the square root of experience no longer carries κ⁻¹, although the additive term still does.

An enhanced algorithm preserves the guarantee while providing constant computational cost, addressing the earlier method's cost growth with episode count. The paper also establishes a lower bound supporting optimality in d and K. This identifies which aspects of the guarantee are optimal while keeping its remaining dependence on the other problem quantities explicit.
neurips-2024-provably-efficient-reinforc.tldr: New multinomial-logit reinforcement-learning algorithms improve regret dependence and computational efficiency, with optimality established in feature dimension and episode count.

paragraphs: Recovering a garment's three-dimensional shape becomes especially difficult when it is folded or otherwise manipulated. Many existing approaches assume clothing is worn, which restricts the shapes they need to represent. This paper addresses the broader range of deformations produced by manipulation, using incomplete three-dimensional point clouds as the observations from which a full shape must be recovered.

The method extends the implicit sewing patterns model with a diffusion-based deformation prior. It maps observed points into UV space, the two-dimensional coordinate space where its priors are learned. The incomplete observations therefore become partial UV maps. Fitting the priors then recovers complete maps together with the mappings from those two-dimensional coordinates into three-dimensional space.

This procedure combines observed geometry with learned information about garment shape and deformation. Experiments report higher reconstruction accuracy than previous methods, especially for the large non-rigid changes caused by manipulation. The findings support extending garment priors beyond the worn-clothing setting so they can represent and reconstruct the more varied shapes encountered during handling.
neurips-2024-reconstruction-of-manipulat.tldr: A diffusion-based deformation prior improves reconstruction of folded and manipulated garments from incomplete three-dimensional observations.

paragraphs: A single-index model projects an input onto one hidden direction and applies a known link function to the result. This paper studies learning that direction when inputs follow a Gaussian distribution and labels may contain adversarial noise. The goal is a computationally efficient learner whose squared-error performance remains competitive with the best model in the specified class.

The authors provide a proper learner, meaning its output remains a single-index model using the given link function. Its error is bounded by a constant multiple of the optimal loss plus an adjustable accuracy term. Sample requirements depend on dimension, desired accuracy, and the link function's information exponent, defined through its first nonzero Hermite coefficient.

The sample bound nearly matches known lower bounds for correlational statistical-query methods, even when those bounds concern noiseless realizable learning. Earlier work either focused on realizable or semi-random-noise settings, or required stronger link-function assumptions for efficient robustness. The contribution is therefore an efficient guarantee under adversarial label noise within the stated Gaussian-input setting.
neurips-2024-sample-and-computationally-.tldr: The paper gives an efficient, noise-robust learner for Gaussian single-index models with error competitive with the best model in its class.

paragraphs: Masked autoencoders learn visual representations through a self-supervised masking process, but their internal learning behavior is not fully understood. This paper analyzes that behavior and finds that the model begins grouping image patches by their patterns surprisingly early in pretraining. The authors use this observation to redesign how the model chooses its masks.

The proposed self-guided masked autoencoder uses its developing patch clusters to generate informed masks. This replaces the random masking used by the original approach. Guidance comes from the model's own progress, so the method does not require an external model or supplementary information to decide which masking patterns to use.

The authors report that this change substantially improves learning, with experiments across multiple downstream vision tasks supporting its effectiveness. The contribution links an observation about what masked autoencoders already learn to a practical modification of their training process. It shows how emerging structure inside a self-supervised learner can provide a useful signal for organizing its own subsequent learning.
neurips-2024-self-guided-masked-autoenco.tldr: Self-guided masked autoencoding uses emerging patch clusters to choose informed masks and improve learning without external supervision.

paragraphs: Automatic prompt optimization can improve either the instructions given to a language model or the examples included in its prompt. These two approaches have largely developed separately, with instruction optimization receiving more recent attention. This paper compares representative methods from both groups, individually and together, across a diverse collection of challenging tasks.

A central finding is that model-generated input-output pairs collected during validation can be reused effectively as prompt examples. Selecting and reusing these pairs consistently improves the instruction-optimization methods studied. The authors also find cases where simple random search over examples, paired with unchanged seed instructions, outperforms state-of-the-art instruction optimization. Example selection can therefore matter more than instruction refinement in the evaluated settings.

The strongest combinations exploit both kinds of optimization: their benefits can reinforce one another rather than merely duplicate effort. These findings support treating example selection as a substantial optimization problem in its own right. They also motivate studying how examples and instructions should be optimized together, even for models that already follow instructions well.
neurips-2024-teach-better-or-show-smarte.tldr: Selecting prompt examples can outperform instruction optimization, and carefully combining both approaches produces stronger results.

paragraphs: Choosing an object detector for a new domain is difficult when images are available but labels are not. Existing domain-adaptation studies often select models using labeled target validation or test data. This paper proposes Detection Adaptation Score, a way to rank trained detectors without target labels and identify models close to the best target-domain choice.

The score approximates whether a model occupies a flat minimum, where small parameter changes produce limited variation. Its Flatness Index Score measures changes in classification and localization after parameter perturbations. A second component, the Prototypical Distance Ratio, assesses transferability and discriminability. A generalization bound connects flatness to model variance and the location of minima to distance between domain distributions.

Together, the components estimate properties relevant to target-domain generalization without directly measuring labeled target accuracy. Experiments across multiple adaptation benchmarks and methods show that the score correlates well with detector performance. The findings support its use for model selection after training, addressing the practical gap between adapting a detector without labels and choosing which adapted detector to deploy.
neurips-2024-towards-unsupervised-model-.tldr: Detection Adaptation Score ranks adapted object detectors without target labels using perturbation stability and measures of transferability and discriminability.

paragraphs: Continually updating a language model requires learning new knowledge while retaining old knowledge. This paper argues that uniformly weighting every training token can cause unnecessary parameter updates and increase forgetting. Instead of treating all tokens as equally useful, the proposed Train-Attention-Augmented Language Model predicts how much each token should contribute to learning.

A meta-learning framework trains these importance predictions, and the resulting token weights guide knowledge updates. The aim is to concentrate training on useful information while reducing changes that undermine previously learned knowledge. This addresses the training procedure itself and can be combined with existing continual-learning approaches such as those focused on retention.

The authors also introduce LAMA-ckl because they find that existing benchmarks do not clearly reveal the trade-off between learning and retaining knowledge. On both new and established benchmarks, TAALM achieves reported state-of-the-art performance relative to the tested baselines. It also shows complementary benefits when integrated with earlier methods, suggesting that better allocation of training attention can strengthen existing approaches.
neurips-2024-train-attention-meta-learni.tldr: TAALM learns token-specific training weights to improve continual knowledge updates while reducing forgetting.

paragraphs: Three-dimensional object detectors using multiple cameras can struggle when moved to a new dataset. Changes in camera perspectives create geometric misalignment between source and target domains, while annotation and training costs constrain adaptation. UDGA combines domain generalization and adaptation to address these obstacles while maintaining useful performance in both domains.

Its Multi-view Overlap Depth Constraint uses relationships between camera views to reduce geometric gaps caused by perspective changes. The framework also introduces label-efficient adaptation for unfamiliar targets, evaluated with target-label amounts of 1% and 5%. This component preserves established source knowledge as part of improving training efficiency during adaptation.

The authors evaluate UDGA on nuScenes, Lyft, and Waymo and report improvements over current state-of-the-art methods. The results support combining geometric consistency across views with adaptation that needs relatively few target annotations. The distinction between the components matters: the framework addresses transfer to unfamiliar data, while its label-efficient adaptation stage explicitly uses a small amount of target supervision.
neurips-2024-unified-domain-generalizati.tldr: UDGA combines multi-view geometric constraints with low-label adaptation to improve three-dimensional detection across domains.

paragraphs: Starting neural-network training with a large learning rate is often associated with better generalization, but the useful range is unclear. This paper conducts a controlled empirical study of how initial learning rates affect final model quality and the kinds of solutions learned. It examines both the geometry of reached minima and the features acquired during training.

The best outcomes occur in a narrow range slightly above the convergence threshold, followed by small-learning-rate fine-tuning or weight averaging. In the studied setting, these initial rates guide optimization into a basin containing only high-quality minima. They also produce a sparse set of learned features concentrated on those most relevant to the task.

Initial rates that are too small instead lead to unstable minima and attempts to learn all features simultaneously, with poorer generalization. Rates that are too large fail to locate good solution basins or extract meaningful patterns. These observations explain why increasing the initial rate can help only within a suitable range in the controlled experiments.
neurips-2024-where-do-large-learning-rat.tldr: A controlled study finds that a narrow initial-learning-rate range favors useful features and good solution basins, while smaller or larger rates perform worse.
